identity.title: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments

problem.claim: Indirect prompt injection can hijack computer-use agents operating across web and OS environments.

gap.claim: Existing evaluations lack realistic controlled adversarial testing or omit hybrid web-OS attack scenarios.

contributions.claim: RedTeamCUA, an adversarial testing framework with a VM-based OS and Docker-based web hybrid sandbox.
RTC-Bench, a benchmark of 864 realistic hybrid web-OS attack examples.
Benchmarking frontier CUAs reveals substantial attack susceptibility and frequent attempts at adversarial tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe the hybrid sandbox as novel and tailor it for configurable red-team scenarios initialized at the injection point.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report an ASR of 42.9% for Claude 3.7 Sonnet | CUA and 7.6% for Operator, the most secure evaluated CUA.
The authors report attempt rates as high as 92.5%, with failures attributed to capability limitations.
The authors report ASRs up to 50% in realistic end-to-end settings.

narrative_sequence.summary: CUAs are presented as vulnerable to indirect prompt injection across web and OS tasks.
Prior evaluations are described as lacking realistic controlled testing or hybrid web-OS coverage.
RedTeamCUA introduces a hybrid sandbox and RTC-Bench with 864 attack examples.
The authors report ASRs of 7.6% for Operator and 42.9% for Claude 3.7 Sonnet | CUA, an Attempt Rate as high as 92.5%, and end-to-end ASRs up to 50%.
The authors call for robust indirect-prompt-injection defenses before deployment.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates attack attempts from completed attack success and reports both metrics.

lessons.interpretation: This distinction exposes failures caused by agent capability limits rather than only resistance to attack.
lessons.application: Report attempt rate alongside success rate when evaluating agent security.
lessons.exception: Attempt rate may be less informative when the evaluation task does not require an explicit agent action.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the complete evaluated CUA set, detailed benchmark construction or splits, statistical uncertainty, or defense baselines.
The reported ASRs' denominators and exact scenario conditions are not provided.
